- 26 days' holiday, rising to 28 days after 2 years' service and 31 days after 5 years' service (pro rated for part time opportunities)
- Option to buy up to 10 days of additional annual leave

- Up to 5 days of carer's leave and 2 paid volunteering days per year

- Learning and development hub where you can access a wealth of resources

- A chance to make a real difference to the lives of our residents

About the Role

As an Administration Assistant within the Partnership Team, you will play an important role in supporting the delivery of domestic fire safety and prevention activity across Surrey.
- Organising and allocating Safe and Well Visits received from partner agencies to Partnership Officers, Partnership Leads and operational crews across Surrey.
- Acting as a first point of contact for members of the public and partner agencies, responding to telephone and written enquiries in a professional and timely manner.
- Supporting the use of internal systems used to record and manage Safe and Well Visits.
- Monitoring activity and producing reports for colleagues and senior leaders within SFRS.
- Supporting the wider Partnership Team and operational crews with a variety of administrative queries and tasks.
- Working closely with Adult Social Care and other partner agencies to help ensure people who may be particularly vulnerable receive appropriate fire safety support.

Prevention is at the heart of Surrey Fire and Rescue Service, and this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on community safety. Through strong organisation, communication and partnership working, you will help ensure vulnerable residents receive the right advice and support, enabling our teams to deliver effective interventions that help people stay safe in their homes.

Over the next 12 to 18 months, you will support the continued delivery and development of Safe and Well Visits across Surrey. Working within the Partnership Team, you will help manage referrals efficiently, ensure accurate and timely information is shared with operational teams and partner agencies, and contribute to improving administrative processes, reporting and the effective use of internal systems to support prevention activity across the Service.

Shortlisting Criteria

In order to be considered for shortlisting, your application will clearly evidence the following skills and align with our behaviours:
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage a varied workload effectively.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Confidence communicating with members of the public, colleagues and partner organisations.
- Experience of working with people from a range of backgrounds, including individuals who may require additional support.
- Ability to work effectively as part of a team and take a proactive approach to completing tasks.
- Confidence using Microsoft Office applications such as Word, Excel and Teams, with the ability and willingness to learn new systems.
- Good attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records and information.

To apply, we request that you submit a CV and you will be asked the following 4 questions:
- Please tell us about your experience of organising and prioritising a varied workload, including how you ensure tasks are completed accurately and on time.
- Please give an example of a time when you communicated with someone who required additional support or assistance. How did you make sure their needs were understood and addressed?
- Please describe your experience of using Microsoft Office applications or other digital systems to manage information, records or reporting.
- Tell us about a time when you worked with colleagues or partner organisations to achieve a positive outcome.

The job advert closes at 23:59 on 18th of October 2026 with interviews planned to follow.

Contact Us

Please contact us for any questions relating to the role. This could be to discuss flexible working requests, transferable skills or any barriers to employment.

Local Government Reorganisation (LGR)

Surrey County Council is undergoing Local Government Reorganisation and will move to new authorities in April 2027. This role is currently employed by Surrey County Council and will remain so until then. If you are employed by Surrey County Council on 1 April 2027, your employment will transfer under TUPE arrangements to one of the new councils, with your current terms and conditions protected. The provisional allocation for this post is Combined Fire and Rescue Authority subject to final confirmation through the wider transition process later this year.

Your skills and experience truly matter to us. From application to your first day, we're committed to supporting you with any adjustments you need, we value inclusion and warmly welcome you to join and help build a workplace where everyone belongs.

The role involves working with a range of stakeholders, including healthcare professionals, managers and external partners. Youll help coordinate information, maintain accurate records and support activities that contribute to a seamless out of hours service. This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and proactive administrator who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, takes pride in delivering high-quality support and can effectively manage a varied workload. This is a 3 month fixed term contract. Maintain effective communication between operational staff, managers and supervisors. Support the Admin Lead with daily administrative and operational tasks. Assist with purchase orders, invoicing processes and supplier administration. Coordinate meetings, manage diaries and arrange appointments with internal and external stakeholders. Maintain accurate records and update information within relevant IT systems. Support recruitment administration and maintain training records and communications. Provide administrative support for projects, meetings and minute taking when required. Carry out general office administration, including telephone reception, filing, printing and scanning. Monitor office supplies and support the efficient running of the service. Assist with operational reporting and the timely processing of service documentation.

title: GP Receptionist
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Receptionist to join the friendly and dedicated team at Upper Halliford Medical Centre. In this role, you will be the first point of contact for patients and visitors, providing an efficient and welcoming reception service both in person and over the phone. We are looking for someone with excellent communication skills, confidence, and a proactive attitude. You should be computer literate, hardworking, eager to learn, and ready to take initiative. Previous experience in a GP practice is desirable but not essential.We value enthusiasm and a positive approach just as much as experience. This is your chance to join a supportive practice where your contribution will be valued and your skills can grow. As a Receptionist, you will be the friendly first point of contact for patients and visitors, helping them access the services they need. You will support the smooth running of the practice by managing appointments, handling enquiries, and assisting with administrative tasks. The role offers variety, patient interaction, and the opportunity to be an essential part of a welcoming, supportive team. Primary Duties: Greet and assist patients and visitors, providing guidance and support as needed Manage the appointment system, including booking, rescheduling, and follow-ups Respond to enquiries in person, by phone, or by email in a professional manner Enter and update patient information accurately on the computer system Assist patients with payments for private services and issue receipts Process new patient registrations and temporary cover documentation Support clinical and administrative staff with general tasks as required Maintain a tidy, organized, and professional reception area Ensure security procedures are followed at the start and end of the day Additional Duties: Assist with scanning, filing, and other document management tasks Support colleagues during staff absences or periods of high workload Follow practice policies on confidentiality, health & safety, and safeguarding Contribute to continuous improvement and efficient service delivery within the team

title: Medical Receptionist/Administrator
description: We are looking to recruit a Medical Secretary to join our busy, friendly and supportive Practice. The hours are 25 hours per week, spread across the week, with the potential for additional hours to cover any team absence. You will need to be articulate, work well within a busy team and use your initiative. You will also need to be efficient, flexible and professional, with extremely good attention to detail. Main purpose of post: To provide secretarial, administrative and reception support to the practice management team, doctors and other clinicians within the practice. Job Responsibilities: Working as part of a team to provide an efficient admin service for GP's and clinicians as required. Reception cover Sending Referrals. To action admin related tasks received into the secretarial/admin team. To action emails received into the practice from patients and other healthcare services. To receive incoming and initiate outgoing telephone calls in order to facilitate timely and appropriate communications with others, taking messages and dealing with appropriate queries and booking appointments. To provide cover for members of the secretarial/admin and reception team during periods of sickness and annual leave. Filing records. Management of referral requests Administration of private patient requests including Insurance, Medical Reports, SARS and Medical Examinations Managing registrations and deductions
